decisions.claim: B has access to a means of telling the current time (e.g., a watch or phone)
decisions.reason: The question 'What time do you have?' carries a presupposition that B has access to a means of telling the current time. Per the rules, definite possessives and presuppositions in questions may establish minimal information. The 'do you have' construction presupposes B possesses a time-telling device (watch, phone, etc.).
decisions.counterexample: B could respond 'I don't have a watch' or 'I don't know,' showing the presupposition is defeasible, but the utterance still minimally presupposes B is expected to have a means of telling time.
